title: Vitello Tonnato
instructions:
Vitello Tonnato

Piedmont veal round marinated in white wine, gently cooked, chilled, and served with tuna, anchovy, egg, and caper sauce.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

For the veal
2 1/4 lb veal eye round
1 1/4 cups dry white wine
1 celery stalk, cut into pieces
2 bay leaves
6 sage leaves
3 whole cloves
2 1/8 qt water, approximately, for cooking
1 2/3 tsp fine salt

For the tuna sauce
about 2 cups drained oil-packed tuna
6 oil-packed anchovy fillets
3 hard-boiled egg yolks
1 heaping tbsp pickled capers, plus 1 tbsp for garnish
juice of 1 lemon
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 tbsp white-wine vinegar
1 cup veal cooking broth, approximately
6 pickled gherkins for serving

Preparation

1. Trim any outer membrane from the veal.

2. Put the meat in a bowl.

3. Pour in the white wine.

4. Add the celery, bay leaves, sage, and cloves.

5. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 12 hours.

6. Transfer the veal to a saucepan.

7. Strain the marinade and pour it over the meat.

8. Add enough water to cover the veal generously.

9. Add the salt.

10. Bring to a boil.

11. Reduce the heat and cook for about 1 hour.

12. Drain the meat, reserving at least 1 cup cooking broth.

13. Cool for 2 hours.

14. Refrigerate for 1 hour so it becomes firm enough to slice thinly.

15. Blend the tuna, yolks, anchovies, capers, lemon juice, olive oil, and vinegar.

16. Gradually add cooking broth until the sauce is smooth and velvety.

17. Slice the veal very thinly.

Service

Arrange the slices on plates, cover generously with tuna sauce, and finish with capers and gherkins.

Chef's note

Chilling the meat completely before slicing produces thin, even slices without tearing the veal.

Carne Cruda All'albese

Fresh Piedmont Fassona beef finely chopped by hand and dressed with extra-virgin olive oil, salt, pepper, and optional lemon and white truffle.

title: Bagna Càuda
instructions:
Bagna Càuda

Warm Piedmont garlic-and-anchovy dip served in individual warmers with raw and cooked vegetables.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 heads garlic, about 40 cloves
10 salt-packed anchovies
2 cups plus 2 tbsp olive oil
1 1/2 tbsp butter
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk, optional for mellowing the garlic

For serving
4 roasted bell peppers
4 cardoons or cardoon ribs
4 small heads radicchio
4 boiled potatoes
4 cooked onions

Preparation

1. Separate the garlic heads into cloves.

2. Peel the cloves and remove the inner germ.

3. For a milder version, put the garlic in a saucepan with the milk.

4. Cook slowly until a fork passes easily through the cloves.

5. Drain and discard the milk.

6. Finely chop the garlic.

7. Desalt and debone the anchovies thoroughly.

8. Put the garlic in a saucepan with about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon olive oil.

9. Add the anchovies.

10. Cook over the lowest possible heat without ever letting the oil boil.

11. Stir continuously for about 10 minutes, until the garlic and anchovies form a uniform mixture.

12. Gradually add the remaining olive oil.

13. Remove from the heat.

14. Stir in the butter.

Service

Transfer to individual warmers and keep hot without frying. Dip the vegetables directly into the sauce.

Chef's note

Bagna càuda should stay hot but never fry. Excessive heat makes both garlic and anchovies bitter.

The long rest softens the anchovies' saltiness and lets the green sauce season them completely.

Lingua al Verde

Cooling the tongue in its broth keeps it moist and makes it easier to peel and slice.

instructions:
Piedmont Russian Salad

Piedmont potato, carrot, pea, tuna, and homemade-mayonnaise salad.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 2 1/3 cups diced potatoes
1 cup diced carrots
1 1/3 cups peas
2 large eggs for garnish
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 tbsp white-wine vinegar
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the mayonnaise
2 egg yolks
about 3/4 cup drained oil-packed tuna
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp sunflower oil
juice of 1/2 lemon
1 tsp mustard
1/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Peel the potatoes and carrots.

2. Cut into 3/16-inch cubes.

3. Boil the potatoes separately in salted water for 6–8 minutes.

4. Boil the carrots separately for 6–8 minutes.

5. Boil the peas for 5 minutes.

6. Immediately chill the peas in ice water.

7. Drain all of the vegetables on a clean kitchen towel.

8. While still warm, dress with the extra-virgin olive oil, vinegar, and salt.

9. Hard-boil the 2 garnish eggs for 8–9 minutes.

10. Cool, peel, and cut into wedges.

11. For the mayonnaise, put the yolks in a bowl with the salt, pepper, and lemon juice.

12. Beat with an electric whisk.

13. Gradually stream in the sunflower oil while whisking continuously.

14. Add the mustard.

15. Finely chop the tuna.

16. Fold it into the mayonnaise.

17. Add the mayonnaise to the vegetables.

18. Mix gently.

19. Cover.

20. Refrigerate for at least 8 hours.

Service

Garnish with the hard-boiled egg wedges and serve cold.

Chef's note

Cutting all of the vegetables to the same size creates an even texture and prevents some pieces from becoming soft before others.

Caponet Piemontesi

3. Blanch the leaves for 3–4 minutes.

5. Thin or remove the toughest central rib.

6. Soak the bread in the milk for 5 minutes.

7. Squeeze lightly.

8. In a bowl, mix the meat, mortadella, Parmigiano, egg, bread, parsley, salt, and pepper.

9. Divide the filling into 12 portions.

10. Put one portion in the center of each leaf.

11. Fold in the sides.

12. Roll into a compact parcel.

Thinning the central rib makes the cabbage leaves flexible enough to close without tearing.

instructions:
Fassona Albese

Paper-thin Piedmont Fassona beef with Parmigiano cream, arugula cream, and dried tomato powder.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb Fassona eye round, completely trimmed
3 1/3 cups Piccadilly or plum tomatoes
about 5 cups finely grated 36-month Parmigiano Reggiano
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp heavy cream
about 20 cups loosely packed arugula
1 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Trim the eye round completely of fat and connective tissue.

2. Wrap tightly in plastic and then foil.

3. Freeze at very low temperature until completely firm.

4. Preheat the oven to 320°F.

5. Cut the tomatoes in half.

6. Arrange on a baking sheet.

7. Bake for 20 minutes.

8. Drain the released liquid.

9. Dry the tomatoes at about 130°F for roughly 12 hours, until completely dry.

10. Grind into a powder.

11. Add about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

12. Blend the arugula with 3/4 cup olive oil until smooth.

13. Add about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

14. Bring the cream almost to a boil.

15. Remove from the heat.

16. Gradually add the grated Parmigiano.

17. Stir until smooth.

18. Cool.

19. Slice the still-firm beef paper-thin on a slicer.

20. Arrange on plates.

21. Let the meat temper for 3–5 minutes.

Service

Finish the Fassona with small amounts of Parmigiano cream, arugula cream, tomato powder, and the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

The beef must remain very cold and firm to produce extremely thin, even slices on the slicer.

5. Remove the garlic.

6. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.

9. Add the pancetta.

10. Brown for 4–5 minutes.

11. Add the black pepper.

12. Add the beans with about 1/2 cup of their liquid.

13. Add the tomato passata.

14. Cook over high heat for 12 minutes.

15. Meanwhile, cook the gnocchetti until al dente.

16. Lift them directly into the skillet with a slotted spoon.

title: Valle D'aosta Crostini
instructions:
Valle D'aosta Crostini

Toasted bread topped with thick Grana cream, cooked ham, and Fontina, then baked until golden.

Yield: 12 crostini

Ingredients

6 crustless sandwich-bread slices, cut in half
12 slices cooked ham
12 slices Fontina
about 1 cup finely grated Grana
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
4 tbsp butter, plus 1 tbsp for browning the bread
1 1/2 cups warm milk
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

2. Heat 1 tablespoon butter with the olive oil in a skillet.

3. Lightly brown the bread halves on both sides.

4. Arrange them in a baking dish.

5. Melt the remaining butter in a saucepan.

6. Add the flour.

7. Stir for 1 minute.

8. Gradually whisk in the warm milk.

9. Add the salt.

10. Cook over low heat until very thick, about 5–7 minutes.

11. Remove from the heat.

12. Stir in the Grana.

13. Spread the cream over the bread.

14. Top each crostino with one slice of ham and one slice of Fontina.

15. Add the nutmeg.

16. Bake for about 15 minutes, until lightly crusted and golden.

Service

Serve immediately while very hot.

Chef's note

The cream should be thicker than ordinary béchamel so it stays on the bread during baking.

Fontina Flans

5. Cool slightly.

6. Divide the Fontina into three portions.

Cool the leeks before adding them to the eggs so the mixture does not begin setting prematurely.

instructions:
Farinata di Ceci

Thin crisp Ligurian chickpea flatbread made with chickpea flour, water, extra-virgin olive oil, and salt.

Ingredients

3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp chickpea flour
1 1/4 cups water
2 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the chickpea flour in a bowl.

2. Gradually add the water while whisking.

3. Continue until the batter is very thin and completely smooth.

4. Cover.

5. Rest for at least 2–3 hours.

6. Skim away any foam from the surface.

7. Add the salt.

8. Mix in 1 tablespoon olive oil.

9. Preheat the oven as hot as possible, about 480°F.

10. Pour the remaining olive oil into a 14-by-8-inch baking pan.

11. Spread it over the bottom.

12. Pour in the batter.

13. Stir gently in the pan so some of the oil disperses through the batter.

14. Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the surface is golden and crisp.

Service

Chef's note

The batter needs its resting time. Fully Balanced the chickpea flour improves both texture and flavor.

title: Fried Ligurian Panissa
instructions:
Fried Ligurian Panissa

Genoese chickpea-flour panissa chilled until firm, cut into pieces, and fried until golden.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 cups chickpea flour
3 cups plus 3 tbsp water
1 tsp fine salt
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Heat the water in a large pot.

2. When it is almost boiling, add the salt.

3. Sift the chickpea flour.

4. Slowly stream it into the water while whisking continuously.

5. Reduce the heat.

6. Cook for at least 15 minutes, stirring often.

7. Once the mixture begins pulling away from the pot, continue for another 5 minutes to dry it.

8. Pour into a deep plate or small baking pan.

9. Smooth to about 3/4 inch thick.

10. Cool completely.

11. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

12. Cut the firm panissa into sticks or rectangles.

13. Heat the oil to 350°F.

14. Fry in small batches until golden and crisp.

15. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately with a small pinch of salt.

Chef's note

Chill the panissa completely before cutting so the pieces hold together during frying.

instructions:
Genoese Cuculli

Genoese chickpea-flour fritters slowly leavened and flavored with fresh herbs.

3/4 cup warm water
1 tsp fresh yeast
2 tbsp finely chopped chives
1 tsp finely chopped rosemary
5 sage leaves, finely chopped
3/4 tsp fine salt
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in 2 tablespoons warm water.

2. Put the chickpea flour in a bowl.

3. Add the dissolved yeast.

4. Gradually add the remaining water.

5. Whisk until the batter is very thick.

6. Add the chives, rosemary, and sage.

7. Cover with a kitchen towel.

8. Let rise at room temperature for 6–8 hours.

9. Alternatively, refrigerate for 12 hours and bring to room temperature for 30 minutes.

10. Add the salt.

11. Stir gently without knocking out all of the air.

12. Heat the oil to 350°F.

13. Scoop the batter by tablespoons.

14. Fry only a few at a time for 5–7 minutes, turning until evenly golden.

15. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve very hot.

Chef's note

The long fermentation develops lightness and flavor. Stir as little as possible after rising so the batter retains its air.

instructions:
Genoese Frisceu

Preparation

1. Measure 3 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon warm water from the total.

2. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in it.

3. Rest for 5–10 minutes.

4. Sift the flour into a bowl.

5. Add the dissolved yeast.

6. Gradually add the remaining water.

7. Whisk until the batter is smooth and thick.

8. Add the extra-virgin olive oil and salt.

9. Fold in the parsley, marjoram, chives, and optional pepper.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise for about 90 minutes.

12. Heat the peanut oil to 340–350°F.

13. Fry 4–5 spoonfuls of batter at a time.

14. Turn during frying.

15. Cook for 3–4 minutes, until puffed and golden.

16. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Do not crowd the pot. Keeping the oil temperature stable is essential for light fritters that do not absorb excess oil.

Ligurian Stuffed Anchovies

Fresh anchovies filled with bread, Parmigiano, capers, garlic, parsley, and marjoram, then baked until golden.

title: Brandacujun
instructions:
Brandacujun

Ligurian stockfish vigorously emulsified with potatoes, onion, garlic, parsley, pine nuts, lemon, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4–6 servings

Ingredients

1 3/4 lb soaked stockfish
4 large potatoes, about 1 3/4 lb, halved
1 onion
1 garlic clove
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/3 cup pine nuts
1 egg yolk
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
juice of 2 lemons
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp ground white pepper, optional

Preparation

1. Put the stockfish in a wide shallow pot with lightly salted cold water.

2. Put the potatoes and onion in a second pot.

3. Bring both pots to a boil.

4. Cook the stockfish, potatoes, and onion for about 30 minutes, until tender.

5. Drain the stockfish.

6. Remove all skin and bones.

7. Break the flesh apart by hand or pound it coarsely in a mortar.

8. Drain the potatoes and onion.

9. Slice them thinly.

10. Finely chop the garlic and parsley.

11. Mix them with the egg yolk, lemon juice, and olive oil.

12. Put the stockfish, potatoes, onion, and pine nuts in a heavy covered pot or bowl.

13. Add the dressing.

14. Season with salt and optional white pepper.

15. Cover tightly.

16. Wrap the container in a kitchen towel.

17. Shake vigorously for several minutes, until creamy and well emulsified.

Service

Serve warm or cold.

Chef's note

Traditional mantecatura is created by shaking the covered vessel. The movement emulsifies the oil, potatoes, and stockfish without turning everything into a purée.

Torta Pasqualina

Ligurian Chard Pie

Ligurian pie with chard, ricotta, prescinseua, porcini, eggs, and marjoram enclosed in multiple paper-thin pastry sheets.

Ingredients

For the filling
2 1/4 lb chard

about 1/3 cup dried porcini

2 cups water
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Soak the porcini in hot water for 20 minutes.

2. Drain, squeeze, and chop.

3. Wash and chop the chard.

4. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a wide skillet.

5. Add the garlic and onion.

6. Cook for 5 minutes.

7. Add the porcini.

8. Add the chard.

9. Sauté for about 10 minutes, until dry.

10. Add the marjoram and salt.

11. Cool completely.

12. For the dough, mix the water, olive oil, and salt.

13. Gradually work in enough flour to form a soft but cohesive dough.

14. Knead for 8–10 minutes.

15. Divide into 10 balls.

16. Rest covered for 30 minutes.

17. Roll each ball paper-thin.

18. Oil and flour a deep baking pan.

19. Line it with 6 overlapping sheets, brushing each lightly with olive oil.

20. Mix the chard with the ricotta and prescinseua.

21. Spread the filling in the pan.

22. Make 4–6 wells.

23. Crack one egg into each.

24. Add the Parmigiano and more marjoram.

25. Cover with the remaining 4 sheets, brushing each with oil.

26. Seal the edges and prick the top.

27. Bake at 350°F for about 1 hour.

Service

Rest for 20 minutes and serve warm.

Chef's note

Roll the pastry nearly transparent. Brushing each individual sheet with oil creates the characteristic delicate flaky structure.

Sardenaira

2 1/2 cups flour

instructions:
Cappon Magro

Ligurian layered seafood dish with sailor crackers, white fish, vegetables, shellfish, and green sauce.

1. Soak the bread for the sauce with the vinegar and 3 tablespoons water.

2. Squeeze lightly.

3. Blend with the anchovies, capers, garlic, yolks, parsley, and salt.

4. Gradually add the olive oil until thick and green.

5. Clean the fish.

6. Steam or gently poach it until just cooked.

7. Cool and remove the bones.

8. Cook the shrimp, mussels, and clams separately.

9. Discard any shellfish that do not open.

10. Boil the carrots, zucchini, potatoes, onions, celery, and green beans separately until al dente.

11. Slice the beet.

12. Dress the fish and each vegetable separately with a little olive oil, vinegar, and salt.

13. Soften the sailor crackers with a little water and vinegar.

14. Line 4 cylindrical molds with plastic wrap.

15. Build layers of cracker, green sauce, vegetables, and fish, pressing lightly.

16. Finish with a cracker.

17. Cover.

18. Place a small weight over each mold.

19. Refrigerate for at least 12 hours, preferably 24.

Service

Turn onto plates, remove the plastic, add more green sauce, and decorate with shrimp, mussels, clams, and beet.

Chef's note

Cooking the vegetables separately preserves the different colors and textures that define the many layers of cappon magro.

Mondeghili

Milanese beef-and-mortadella meatballs flavored with lemon and nutmeg, breaded and cooked in butter.

Nervetti Salad

Sciatt Valtellinesi

12. Drain on paper towels.

Fried Polenta with Gorgonzola

Preparation

1. Bring the milk and water to a boil in a saucepan.

2. Add the salt.

3. Slowly stream in the cornmeal while stirring continuously.

4. Reduce the heat.

5. Cook the polenta for about 1 hour, stirring regularly.

6. Remove from the heat.

7. Stir in the butter.

8. Pour the polenta into a lightly dampened rectangular pan.

9. Smooth to about 3/4 inch thick.

10. Cool completely.

11. Unmold.

12. Cut into squares.

17. Arrange the squares in a baking pan.

18. Top each with Gorgonzola.

Chef's note

The polenta must be completely cold and firm before frying or the squares can break apart in the oil.

Sardinian Gnocchetti with Clams and Zucchini Cream

Preparation

1. Discard any broken clams.

2. Rinse the clams.

3. Soak them in cold salted water for 2 hours.

4. Drain and rinse.

5. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a wide skillet.

6. Add 1 crushed garlic clove and the parsley stems.

7. Add the clams.

8. Cover and cook until they open, about 3–5 minutes.

9. Discard any clams that remain closed.

10. Shell most of the clams, reserving several whole for serving.

11. Strain the clam liquid very carefully.

12. Cut only the green outer portion of the zucchini into thin batons.

13. Blanch for 30 seconds.

14. Chill immediately in ice water.

15. Blend the zucchini with the almonds, 1 tablespoon olive oil, and 1/4–1/2 cup clam liquid until thick and smooth.

16. Clean the squash blossoms and remove the pistils.

17. Cut them into strips.

18. Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a boil.

19. Cook the gnocchetti until 2 minutes short of al dente.

20. Warm the zucchini cream in a wide skillet.

21. Add the pepper and lemon zest.

22. Transfer the gnocchetti to the cream with 1/4 cup pasta water.

23. Finish cooking for 2 minutes.

24. Add the clams and squash blossoms.

25. Toss for 30 seconds.

Finish with the whole clams, chopped parsley, and remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

Strain the clam liquid through cheesecloth or a very fine filter so residual sand does not enter the zucchini cream.

Gnocco Fritto

Emilia-Romagna fried dough made with flour, milk, water, and lard, then fried in lard until puffed.

Preparation

1. Measure 2 teaspoons water and 2 teaspoons milk from the total.

2. Dissolve the yeast in those liquids.

3. Combine the two flours in a bowl.

4. Add the lard.

5. Work briefly with your fingertips.

6. Add the dissolved yeast.

7. Gradually add the remaining water and milk.

8. Add the sugar.

9. Add the salt last.

10. Transfer to the work surface.

11. Knead for 5–10 minutes, until smooth.

12. Form a ball.

13. Cover.

14. Let rise for about 90 minutes.

15. Divide the dough into portions.

16. Roll to about 1/16 inch thick.

17. Cut into irregular diamonds or squares.

18. Melt the frying lard in a wide pot.

19. Heat to 375°F.

20. Fry only a few pieces at a time.

21. Turn them once they puff.

22. Drain on absorbent paper.

Service

Serve immediately with cured meats, cheeses, or pickles.

Chef's note

Thin dough and high frying heat allow gnocco fritto to puff quickly without absorbing excessive fat.

23. Cover the filling, creating slight wrinkles in the pastry.

instructions:
Wild Hop Frittata

Piedmont frittata with wild hop shoots and Parmigiano.

Ingredients

about 8 cups tender wild hop shoots
8 large eggs
1 cup finely grated Parmigiano
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Trim the hop shoots, removing the toughest lower stems.

2. Wash thoroughly.

3. Cut into pieces 1–1 1/4 inches long.

4. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a nonstick skillet.

5. Add the hop shoots.

6. Cook over low heat for 5–7 minutes, until wilted.

7. Transfer to a bowl.

8. Beat the eggs.

9. Add the Parmigiano, salt, and pepper.

10. Stir in the hop shoots.

11. Heat the remaining olive oil in the same skillet.

12. Pour in the mixture.

13. Cook over medium heat for 5–6 minutes.

14. Turn the frittata with the help of a plate or lid.

15. Cook the second side for 4–5 minutes.

Wild hop shoots need only brief preliminary cooking. Prolonged cooking dulls their fresh green character.

Supplì al Telefono

Roman ragù rice croquettes with a stretchy mozzarella center, breaded and fried.

1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For breading and frying
2 large eggs
about 1 2/3 cups breadcrumbs
4 1/4 cups peanut oil

Preparation

1. Soak the dried mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes.

2. Drain, squeeze, and chop.

3. Melt 2 tablespoons butter with the olive oil in a saucepan.

4. Add the onion.

5. Cook for 5 minutes.

6. Add the ground beef.

7. Brown for 5–6 minutes.

8. Add the chicken livers and mushrooms.

9. Cook for another 5 minutes.

10. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate.

11. Add the passata.

12. Season with salt and pepper.

13. Cook until reduced, about 15 minutes.

14. Add the rice.

15. Cook, gradually adding the hot broth.

16. Turn off the heat.

17. Stir in the finishing butter and Grana.

18. Add the 2 beaten eggs.

19. Spread the rice on a large tray.

20. Cool completely for about 2 hours.

21. Cut the mozzarella into batons and pat dry.

22. With wet hands, take one portion of rice.

23. Put mozzarella in the center.

24. Shape into a compact oval croquette.

25. Dip first in the 2 beaten eggs and then in breadcrumbs.

26. Heat the oil to 350°F.

27. Fry in small batches until deeply golden.

28. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve very hot so the mozzarella forms the characteristic long strand.

Chef's note

The rice must be completely cold before shaping. Warm rice is too soft to enclose the mozzarella cleanly.

Fried Salt Cod Fillets

4. Mix the flour and yeast.

Roman Panzanella

Tuscan Donzelle

Tuscan chestnut-flour crêpes cooked on a griddle and filled with fresh ricotta.

Tuscan Cecina

Thin Tuscan chickpea flatbread made with chickpea flour, water, extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and pepper.

4 1/4 cups water

2 1/2 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Put the chickpea flour in a large bowl.

2. Gradually whisk in the water until the batter is smooth and very thin.

3. Add the salt.

4. Cover and rest for at least 4 hours.

5. During resting, skim away any foam that rises to the surface.

6. Add the olive oil and whisk vigorously.

7. Preheat the oven as hot as possible, at least 480°F.

8. Coat a wide shallow pan generously with the remaining olive oil.

9. Pour in the batter in a thin layer.

10. Bake until deeply golden and beginning to char lightly, about 12–18 minutes.

11. Finish with black pepper.

Service

Cut into pieces and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Cecina should be very thin. A wide pan promotes a crisp crust and prevents the center from staying overly soft.

Chicken Liver Crostini

Keeping a little cooking liquid before blending creates a smooth spread without requiring extra fat.

Tuscan Panzanella

1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Squeezing the bread well prevents a watery salad and helps the olive oil cling to the ingredients.

Lumachelle Orvietane

Orvieto spiral rolls with pancetta, cheese, olive oil, and black pepper.

Yield: about 24 pieces

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 cup plus 3 tbsp warm water
about 1 2/3 cups diced pancetta
1 cup finely grated Parmigiano or Pecorino
1 1/2 tbsp lard
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
about 1 1/2 tsp fresh yeast
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Put the flour in a bowl.

2. Crumble the yeast into the center.

3. Gradually add the warm water.

4. Knead at moderate speed or by hand.

5. Add the olive oil, lard, cheese, and pancetta.

6. Add the salt and pepper.

7. Knead for about 15 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise until at least doubled, about 2–3 hours.

10. Divide into portions of about 3 tablespoons each.

11. Roll into long thin ropes.

12. Coil each rope into a loose spiral.

13. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

14. Let rise for another 20–30 minutes.

title: Crescia Sfogliata
instructions:
Crescia Sfogliata

Layered Marche flatbread made with lard and black pepper, cooked on a griddle and served with Carpegna prosciutto, Casciotta d'Urbino, and optional sautéed greens.

Yield: 6 flatbreads

Ingredients

For the dough
4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
2 medium eggs
1/2 cup plus 1–2 tbsp warm water
3 1/2 tbsp softened lard
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For layering
5 1/2 tbsp softened lard

For filling
about 1 2/3 cups sliced Carpegna prosciutto
about 1 2/3 cups sliced Casciotta d'Urbino
about 6 cups cooked sautéed field greens, optional

Preparation

1. Put the flour, eggs, softened lard, salt, and pepper in a bowl.

2. Gradually add the warm water.

3. Knead by hand for about 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

4. Wrap and rest for 30–60 minutes.

5. Divide the dough into 6 balls.

6. Roll each into a thin disk.

7. Brush each disk with softened lard.

8. Roll into a cigar.

9. Coil the cigar into a spiral.

10. Rest for 30 minutes.

11. Roll each spiral into a thin disk again.

12. Heat a griddle or testo over medium-high heat.

13. Cook each crescia for about 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and layered.

14. Tap or gently twist the hot crescia to separate the layers.

Service

Fill immediately with prosciutto, Casciotta, and optional sautéed greens.

Chef's note

The second rest after coiling relaxes the gluten so the dough can be rolled again without tearing the lard layers.

instructions:
Olive All'ascolana

title: Fried Custard Cubes
instructions:
Fried Custard Cubes

Very firm pastry-cream cubes double-breaded and fried until golden.

Yield: about 40 pieces

For the custard
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk

2. Beat the yolks with the sugar.

3. Add the cornstarch and flour.

4. Strain the hot milk and gradually whisk it into the yolks.

5. Return everything to the heat.

6. Cook, stirring, until the custard becomes very firm.

7. Pour into a baking pan.

8. Smooth to about 1 1/4 inches thick.

9. Cool for about 2 hours without covering the surface with plastic.

10. Turn the custard onto a cutting board.

11. Cut into cubes.

12. Coat each cube in breadcrumbs.

13. Dip in beaten egg.

14. Coat again in breadcrumbs.

15. Heat the oil to 350°F.

16. Fry only a few cremini at a time, turning until evenly golden.

17. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Ciauscolo with Crescia

Warm layered Marche flatbread served with ciauscolo and Casciotta d'Urbino.

For the crescia
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
5 1/2 tbsp lard, plus 4 tbsp for layering

1 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp baking soda, optional

For filling
about 2 cups sliced ciauscolo
about 1 2/3 cups sliced Casciotta d'Urbino

Preparation

1. Put the flour, lard, salt, and optional baking soda in a bowl.

2. Gradually add the warm water.

3. Knead until smooth and elastic.

4. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

5. Divide into 4 portions.

6. Roll each into a thin disk.

7. Brush with the layering lard.

8. Roll each disk into a cylinder.

9. Coil the cylinder into a spiral.

10. Rest for 20 minutes.

11. Roll out again.

12. Heat a griddle or testo.

13. Cook for about 2–3 minutes per side, until golden.

14. Slice the ciauscolo and Casciotta.

Service

Chef's note

Filling the crescia immediately after cooking lets the residual heat soften the ciauscolo and cheese without actually cooking them.

Marche Salt Cod Fritters

6. Gradually whisk in the ice water.

7. Continue until smooth.

8. Add the salt cod.

9. Add the pepper and taste before adding salt.

10. Cover.

11. Rest for 20 minutes.

13. Scoop spoonfuls of batter.

14. Fry only a few at a time for 6–7 minutes, turning often.

15. Drain on paper towels.

Salt cod retains natural salinity even after desalting, so add salt only after tasting the batter.

instructions:
Abruzzo Cheese Bread

Abruzzo Easter bread rich with Pecorino, Parmigiano, and semisoft aged cheese.

Yield: 8–10 servings

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
2/3 cup warm water

3 large eggs
about 2 cups finely grated Pecorino Romano
about 1 1/2 cups finely grated Parmigiano
about 1 1/4 cups diced semisoft aged cheese
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp milk
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 tsp sugar

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water with the sugar.

2. Combine the flour, salt, pepper, Pecorino, and Parmigiano.

3. Add the dissolved yeast.

4. Add the 3 eggs.

5. Add the milk.

6. Knead until the dough begins to come together.

7. Gradually add the butter in small pieces.

8. Continue until fully absorbed.

9. Add the diced semisoft cheese.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise for 2 hours or until doubled.

12. Fold the dough over itself several times.

13. Form a ball.

14. Transfer to a buttered tall 2-pound bread mold.

15. Let rise for about 1 hour.

16. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

17. Brush with the beaten egg.

18. Bake for 40–45 minutes.

19. Cool before unmolding.

Service

Serve sliced, preferably at room temperature.

Chef's note

Add the butter only after the dough has begun developing so the gluten structure stays elastic.

instructions:
Pallotte Cacio e Ova

Abruzzo bread, Parmigiano, Pecorino, and egg balls fried and then simmered in tomato sauce.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the balls
about 2 1/2 cups fresh bread crumb
3/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
3/4 cup finely grated Pecorino Romano
6 medium eggs
1 garlic clove, minced
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

For the sauce
4 1/4 cups tomato passata
1/3 cup finely chopped white onion
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
6 basil leaves
1/2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Mix the bread crumb, Parmigiano, Pecorino, garlic, parsley, and pepper.

2. Beat the eggs separately.

3. Add them to the mixture.

4. Mix until soft and uniform.

5. Cover.

6. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

7. Form balls about 2 tablespoons each.

8. Coat lightly in flour.

9. Heat the oil to 350°F.

10. Fry only a few at a time until golden.

11. Drain on paper towels.

12. For the sauce, heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a saucepan.

13. Add the onion.

14. Cook until soft.

15. Add the passata, basil, and salt.

16. Cook for 15 minutes.

17. Arrange the fried balls in the sauce in a single layer.

18. Cover with a small vent.

19. Simmer over low heat for about 30 minutes.

Service

Serve very hot with plenty of sauce.

Chef's note

Chilling the mixture firms it so the balls are easier to shape and less likely to open while frying.

Abruzzo Salt Cod Fritters

Abruzzo potato-enriched yeasted fritters with a piece of salt cod sealed inside.

2 tbsp beaten egg
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp olive oil
about 3/4 cup desalted soaked salt cod pieces

Preparation

1. Cut the potatoes into small cubes.

2. Boil until tender.

3. Drain, reserving a little cooking water.

4. Mash the potatoes with about 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon of their cooking water.

5. Put the flour, potato purée, and yeast in a bowl.

6. Add the salt, olive oil, and egg.

7. Gradually add the water.

8. Knead for 5–6 minutes.

9. Beat the dough vigorously for about 1 minute.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise until doubled, about 90 minutes.

12. Cut the salt cod into small pieces.

13. Heat the oil to 350°F.

14. Lightly oil your hands.

15. Take a small portion of dough.

16. Flatten it in your palm.

17. Put one piece of salt cod in the center.

18. Close the dough around it to form a ball.

19. Fry only a few at a time until puffed and golden.

20. Drain on paper towels.

Chef's note

The dough should remain soft and slightly sticky. Oil your hands instead of adding extra flour, which would make the fritters heavy.

instructions:
Antipasto alla Giuliese

Giulianova seafood appetizer with shrimp, sole, squid, and clams served with tuna, anchovy, caper, and green-pepper sauce.

juice of 1 lemon

Preparation

1. Rinse the clams.

2. Clean the squid and sole.

3. Shell the shrimp.

4. Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil.

5. Cook the shrimp, sole, squid, and clams separately, removing each ingredient as soon as it is done.

6. Discard any clams that do not open.

7. Let everything cool.

8. Dress the seafood with the olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, and salt.

9. For the sauce, finely chop the garlic and parsley.

10. Put the tuna, anchovies, capers, and green pepper in a blender.

11. Add the garlic-parsley mixture.

12. Blend while adding the olive oil and vinegar until smooth and fluid.

Service

Arrange the seafood salad on plates and serve the sauce alongside or spooned lightly over the seafood.

Chef's note

Cooking each seafood separately prevents the squid and shrimp from becoming rubbery while waiting for the other ingredients to finish.

title: Scapece alla Vastese

Scapece alla Vastese

Abruzzo fried fish marinated for at least one day in white-wine vinegar infused with saffron.

Yield: 8 servings

1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
4 1/4 cups white-wine vinegar
about 1/2 tsp saffron threads
3 cups plus 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for frying

Preparation

1. Clean the fish.

2. Cut into even pieces.

3. Dry very thoroughly.

4. Coat each piece lightly in flour.

5. Heat the oil to 350°F.

6. Fry the fish in batches until golden.

7. Drain on paper towels.

8. Season lightly with salt.

9. Heat the vinegar in a nonreactive saucepan until almost boiling.

10. Briefly toast the saffron threads on a warm spoon.

11. Crush them finely.

12. Remove the vinegar from the heat.

13. Add the saffron.

14. Layer the fried fish in a glass or earthenware container.

15. Pour the saffron vinegar over the fish until completely covered.

16. Cool.

Service

Drain the fish lightly from the marinade and serve cold or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Keep the fish fully submerged in the saffron vinegar during marination so it seasons evenly.

Pampanella

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Cut the pork into thick slices without cutting completely through if using a whole loin section.

3. Mix the garlic, sweet pepper, hot pepper, and salt.

4. Rub the seasoning over every surface and into the cuts.

5. Arrange the pork in a roasting pan.

6. Cover with damp parchment and then foil.

7. Roast for about 1 hour 50 minutes.

8. Remove the covering.

9. Drain excess water and fat from the pan.

10. Drizzle with the vinegar.

5. Slowly rotate the caciocavallo so the lower surface heats evenly.

6. When the rind begins to soften and the cheese underneath melts, hold one bread slice beneath it.

8. Gradually lower the caciocavallo as it is consumed, always keeping it about 4 inches from the coals.

5. Cook for about 10 minutes, like a soft polenta.

title: Mozzarella in Carrozza
instructions:
Mozzarella in Carrozza

Neapolitan fried mozzarella sandwiches made with white bread, mozzarella, eggs, and crisp breading.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

8 slices sandwich bread
about 1 2/3 cups well-drained mozzarella
2 large eggs
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp milk
1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 1/4 cups breadcrumbs
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
3 cups plus 3 tbsp peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Drain the mozzarella for at least 1 hour.

2. Cut into slices about 3/16 inch thick.

3. Remove the crusts from the bread.

4. Make 4 sandwiches with the mozzarella, leaving a small border around the edges.

5. Press the edges firmly.

6. Pour the milk into one shallow dish.

7. Put the flour in a second dish.

8. Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper in a third dish.

9. Put the breadcrumbs in a fourth dish.

10. Lightly moisten the sandwich edges with milk.

11. Coat each sandwich in flour.

12. Dip in egg.

13. Coat completely in breadcrumbs.

14. Heat the oil to 340–350°F.

15. Fry for 1–2 minutes per side, until golden.

16. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately while very hot.

Chef's note

Draining the mozzarella thoroughly is essential so its moisture does not burst through the breading while frying.

instructions:
Neapolitan Pasta Frittatina

Neapolitan bucatini fritters with béchamel, ham, peas, and Parmigiano, battered and fried.

Yield: about 16 pieces

Ingredients

about 2 cups dry bucatini
about 2/3 cup diced cooked ham
1/3 cup peas
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 tsp fine salt

For the béchamel
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp milk
2 tbsp butter
3 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 pinch freshly grated nutmeg
1/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp ground white pepper

For the batter
3/4 cup plus 3 tbsp water
1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour

For frying
4 1/4 cups peanut oil

Preparation

1. Melt the butter in a saucepan.

2. Add the flour.

3. Cook for 1 minute.

4. Gradually whisk in the milk.

5. Cook until the béchamel is very thick.

6. Season with nutmeg, salt, and white pepper.

7. Cook the bucatini in salted water until al dente.

8. Drain.

9. While hot, mix with the béchamel, ham, peas, and Parmigiano.

10. Press the mixture firmly into a pan or container.

11. Refrigerate for 3 hours.

12. Cut rounds with a cutter about 2 1/2 inches wide.

13. Press the scraps together and cut additional rounds.

14. Mix the water and flour into a smooth batter.

15. Heat the oil to 350°F.

16. Batter only 2–3 rounds at a time.

17. Fry for about 2 minutes.

18. Drain briefly.

19. Fry a second time for another 2 minutes, until golden.

20. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

The long refrigeration firms the pasta mixture enough to cut and batter cleanly without breaking.

instructions:
Neapolitan Potato Croquettes

Neapolitan potato croquettes with Parmigiano, butter, and parsley, breaded and fried.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb potatoes
2 egg yolks
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
2 tbsp butter
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley

1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For breading
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour

1 large egg

For frying

Preparation

1. Put the whole unpeeled potatoes in cold salted water.

2. Bring to a boil.

3. Cook for 30–40 minutes, until tender.

4. Drain.

5. Peel while still hot.

6. Pass through a potato ricer.

7. Cool slightly.

8. Add the yolks, Parmigiano, butter, parsley, salt, and pepper.

9. Mix well.

10. Rest for 30 minutes.

11. Shape into elongated croquettes with lightly damp hands.

12. Coat in flour.

13. Beat the egg whites with the whole egg.

14. Dip the croquettes in the egg mixture.

15. Coat in breadcrumbs.

16. Heat the oil to 350°F.

17. Fry only a few croquettes at a time until golden.

Chef's note

Use dry, floury potatoes so the mixture does not require extra flour and the centers stay fluffy.

title: Marinated Anchovies

Marinated Anchovies

Neapolitan anchovies marinated in white-wine vinegar and dressed with olive oil, parsley, garlic, and optional chile.

Yield: 5 servings

3 cups plus 3 tbsp white-wine vinegar
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 tsp fine salt
1 small chile, thinly sliced, optional

Preparation

1. Clean the anchovies, removing the heads, innards, and central bones.

2. Open them flat.

3. Rinse briefly.

4. Dry thoroughly.

5. Arrange the anchovies in a nonreactive container in one or more layers.

6. Pour in enough vinegar to cover them completely.

7. Cover.

8. Refrigerate for about 3 hours.

9. Drain away all of the vinegar.

10. Pat the anchovies dry gently.

11. Arrange them in the container again.

12. Dress with the olive oil, garlic, parsley, salt, and optional chile.

13. Cover.

14. Refrigerate for another 2 hours.

Service

Let stand at room temperature for 10 minutes before serving.

Chef's note

Use anchovies suitable for raw consumption or previously frozen according to applicable parasite-control guidance, because vinegar marination does not replace that treatment.

Drying the anchovies thoroughly before flouring helps the coating adhere and reduces splattering in the oil.

title: Peppered Mussels
instructions:
Peppered Mussels

Neapolitan mussels opened with white wine and served with a butter, shallot, garlic, parsley, and black-pepper sauce.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

3 3/4 lb mussels
5 1/2 tbsp butter
1 shallot, finely chopped
1 garlic clove, crushed
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 cup strained mussel liquid
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/3 tsp fine salt, only if needed

Preparation

1. Clean the mussels thoroughly, removing beards and shell debris.

2. Discard broken mussels or open ones that do not close when tapped.

3. Put the mussels in a large pot over high heat.

4. Add the wine.

5. Cover.

6. Cook over medium-low heat for 5–7 minutes, shaking the pot, until the mussels open.

7. Discard any that remain closed.

8. Remove the mussels from the pot.

9. Strain the cooking liquid carefully and measure 1 cup.

10. Melt the butter in a skillet over low heat.

11. Add the shallot and garlic.

12. Cook for 3–4 minutes without browning.

13. Add the flour.

14. Stir for 1 minute.

15. Gradually add the mussel liquid, stirring to prevent lumps.

16. Return the mussels to the sauce.

17. Add the black pepper and parsley.

18. Taste before adding any salt.

Service

Serve immediately with plenty of the cooking sauce.

Chef's note

The natural mussel liquid is already quite salty, so add salt only after tasting the finished sauce.

Polpo alla Luciana

1. Rinse and dry the octopus.

2. Heat the olive oil in a heavy saucepan.

3. Add the garlic, cherry tomatoes, and half of the parsley.

4. Cook for 3–4 minutes.

5. Add the olives and capers.

6. Cook for 2 minutes.

7. Add the tomato passata.

8. Bring to a boil.

9. Lower the whole octopus into the sauce.

10. Return to a gentle boil.

11. Reduce the heat to the lowest setting.

12. Cover.

13. Cook for about 1 hour, turning the octopus gently halfway through.

14. Check tenderness by inserting a fork into the thickest part of a tentacle.

15. Add the salt only at the end of cooking.

16. Add the remaining parsley.

Service

Serve hot with plenty of sauce and bread.

Chef's note

Keep the cooking very gentle and covered. The octopus releases its own liquid and stays tender without added water.

title: Escarole Pie
instructions:
Escarole Pie

Neapolitan stuffed pizza with escarole, anchovies, pine nuts, and raisins.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
5 cups all-purpose flour
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast
2/3 cup milk
2/3 cup warm water, divided
2 1/2 tsp fine salt

For the filling
2 large heads escarole, about 2 2/3 lb
about 1/4 cup oil-packed anchovies
3 tbsp pine nuts
2 tbsp raisins
1 garlic clove
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For brushing
1 egg yolk
1 tbsp milk

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in 3 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon warm water.

2. Put the flour in a bowl.

3. Add the dissolved yeast, milk, and remaining water.

4. Knead until the ingredients begin coming together.

5. Add the salt.

6. Continue kneading until smooth and uniform.

7. Form a ball.

8. Cover and let rise for about 2 hours.

9. Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes.

10. Drain and squeeze dry.

11. Clean the escarole.

12. Cut into pieces about 1 1/4 inches wide.

13. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet.

14. Add the garlic.

15. Cook for 1 minute, then remove it.

16. Add the anchovies.

17. Stir until they begin dissolving.

18. Add the escarole, raisins, and pine nuts.

19. Season with salt and pepper.

20. Cook for about 5 minutes.

21. Drain away the released liquid thoroughly.

22. Cool completely.

23. Divide the dough into two pieces.

24. Roll the first piece and line a greased round baking pan.

25. Add the cooled filling.

26. Roll the second piece.

27. Cover and seal the edges carefully.

28. Prick the surface.

29. Beat the egg yolk with the milk.

30. Brush the top.

31. Bake in a preheated 350°F oven for about 45 minutes.

Service

Rest for 15 minutes and serve hot, warm, or cold.

instructions:
Neapolitan Casatiello

Neapolitan Easter bread filled with salami, provolone, pork cracklings, Pecorino, and Parmigiano, with whole eggs baked into the top.

For the dough
8 1/3 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
2 1/2 cups water, room temperature
about 1 cup lard

about 3 1/3 cups diced Neapolitan salami

about 1 cup plus 2 tbsp finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano

5 whole raw eggs in their shells

Preparation

1. Combine the flour and yeast.

2. Gradually add the water while kneading.

3. Gradually work in the lard.

4. Add the salt.

7. Form a ball.

8. Cover and let rise for 3 hours.

9. Dice the salami, provolone, and cracklings.

10. Reserve about 1 cup of dough for the decorative strips.

11. Roll the remaining dough into a large rectangle.

12. Distribute the salami, provolone, cracklings, Pecorino, Parmigiano, and pepper.

13. Roll up from the long side into a cylinder.

14. Grease a ring pan about 12 1/2 inches wide with some of the lard.

15. Arrange the cylinder in the pan.

16. Join and seal the ends.

17. Set the 5 raw eggs into the top.

18. Roll the reserved dough into 10 thin ropes.

19. Cross two ropes over each egg.

20. Continue rising until at least 4 total hours have elapsed.

21. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

22. Brush the top with the remaining lard.

23. Bake for about 60 minutes.

Service

Cool slightly before unmolding and slicing.

The raw eggs cook in their shells with the casatiello. Secure them well with the dough strips so they do not move during rising and baking.

Neapolitan Tortano

Classic Neapolitan Easter bread with lard, mixed cured meats, cheeses, Pecorino, and black pepper.

For the dough
5 3/4 cups plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour

1 tsp sugar
2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For the pan and top

Preparation

2. Put the flour in a bowl.

3. Add the yeast water.

4. Gradually add the remaining 1 1/4 cups water.

5. Work in the lard gradually.

6. Add the salt and black pepper.

7. Knead vigorously for about 10 minutes, until smooth.

8. Form a ball.

9. Cover and let rise for about 2 hours, until well expanded.

10. Dice the cured meats and cheeses.

11. Roll the dough into a rectangle about 3/8 inch thick.

12. Distribute the meats, cheeses, and Pecorino over the entire surface.

13. Roll from the long side.

14. Grease an 11-inch ring pan with half of the lard.

15. Put the roll in the pan.

16. Join and seal the ends.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 375°F.

19. Brush the top with the remaining lard.

20. Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes.

22. Continue for about 45 minutes.

Service

Cool slightly before unmolding and slicing.

Chef's note

The second rise should be long because the rich fatty filling naturally slows the dough's expansion.

Pasta Cresciuta Fritters

Neapolitan spoonfuls of very soft yeasted dough fried until puffed and golden.

Yield: 20–30 fritters

Ingredients

2 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp warm water
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a bowl.

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Mix vigorously with a fork or sturdy whisk.

5. Add the salt last.

6. Continue mixing until the dough is smooth, uniform, and very soft.

7. Cover.

8. Let rise until at least doubled, about 2 hours.

9. Heat the oil to 350–355°F.

10. Dip two spoons in the hot oil.

11. Scoop a small amount of dough.

12. Slide it into the oil.

13. Fry only a few fritters at a time without letting them touch.

14. Turn during frying.

15. Remove once evenly golden, about 3–4 minutes.

16. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

The dough should be softer than pizza dough. Do not add extra flour to make it easier to handle; use lightly oiled spoons instead.

instructions:
Taralli ’Nzogna e Pepe

Neapolitan lard-and-black-pepper taralli with toasted almonds.

Yield: 20–30 taralli

Ingredients

For the starter
1 1/3 cups type 0 or bread flour
about 2 1/2 tsp fresh yeast
1/3 cup water

3/4 cup water
1 cup plus 1 tbsp lard
about 2 3/4 cups whole unpeeled almonds
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
2 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
1 tsp sugar

Preparation

1. Mix the water, yeast, and starter flour.

2. Form a soft starter.

3. Dust lightly with flour.

4. Cover and let double for about 1 hour.

5. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

6. Toast the almonds for 2–5 minutes.

7. Cool.

8. Reserve about one-third of the almonds whole.

9. Coarsely chop the rest.

10. Put the dough flour in a bowl.

11. Add the starter, water, pepper, lard, salt, sugar, and chopped almonds.

12. Knead until uniform.

13. Form thin ropes.

14. Twist them together in pairs.

15. Close each pair into a ring.

16. Decorate with the reserved whole almonds.

17. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

18. Let rise for about 1 hour.

19. Bake in a convection oven at 350°F for 10 minutes.

20. Reduce to 320°F.

21. Continue for 35–40 minutes.

22. Turn off the oven.

23. Leave the taralli inside with the door slightly open for 10 minutes.

Service

Cool completely before serving.

Chef's note

The final drying period in the turned-off oven makes the taralli especially crisp and crumbly.

Lucanian Acquasale

1 onion

1 tsp dried oregano
1/2 hot chile, minced

3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Finely chop the onion and celery.

2. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan.

3. Add the onion, celery, oregano, chile, and half of the salt.

4. Sauté for 2 minutes.

5. Add the water.

8. Crack the eggs directly into the broth.

9. Stir with a fork or whisk to scramble them.

5. Add the remaining water only if the bread is still too dry.

Service

title: Puglian Panzerotti
instructions:
Puglian Panzerotti

Fried Puglian half-moons filled with tomato, mozzarella, and Parmigiano.

Yield: about 16 panzerotti

Ingredients

For the dough
8 1/3 cups all-purpose flour
1 2/3 cups warm water
about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
1 tsp sugar
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 3 1/3 cups well-drained diced mozzarella
1 1/4 cups tomato passata
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For frying
8 1/2 cups peanut oil

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Knead until the dough begins to become uniform.

5. Add the salt.

6. Continue kneading for 10–15 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

7. Cover.

8. Let rise for about 2 hours, until doubled.

9. Meanwhile, mix the tomato passata, mozzarella, Parmigiano, olive oil, salt, and pepper.

10. Refrigerate the filling for 30 minutes.

11. Divide the dough into 16 portions.

12. Shape into balls.

13. Cover.

14. Let rise for another hour.

15. Roll each ball into a disk 4 3/4–6 inches wide.

16. Put about 2 tablespoons filling on one half.

17. Fold into a half-moon.

18. Press the edges firmly with your fingers.

19. Seal with the tines of a fork.

20. Heat the oil to 350–355°F.

21. Fry only one or two panzerotti at a time.

22. Turn during frying.

23. Remove when puffed and deeply golden, about 3–4 minutes.

24. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Keep the filling cold and drain the mozzarella thoroughly. A wet filling makes the panzerotti difficult to seal and can cause them to open while frying.
